goal: Add an automatic table of contents
preamble: A table of contents in Docs isn't something you write — it's something Docs builds for you, from your headings. So the real task is teaching Docs which lines are headings. That's what styles are for.
generalization: You never touched the table of contents itself — it built itself from your headings. That's the whole point of styles: they describe what text *is*, not what it looks like. It's also why the outline pane on the left already works now, and why exporting to PDF will keep your structure.

steps.intent: This box in the toolbar always shows the style of whatever line your cursor is on. Right now it says 'Normal text'. Watch it as I move around.
hints: It's in the toolbar, left of the font name.

steps.intent: Click anywhere on the document's title line. You won't see anything change in the document — watch the Styles box instead.
hints: The very first line of the document.
Top of the page, the big line of text.

steps.intent: Now open the Styles dropdown. This is where you tell Docs what kind of line this is.
hints: Toolbar, just right of the undo/redo arrows.

wrongHints.Font: That's the typeface — it changes how text looks. We want to change what the text *is*.
wrongHints.Font size: Size is cosmetic. Styles carry meaning, which is what a table of contents reads.

steps.intent: Choose Heading 1. You're telling Docs 'this line is a top-level section'.
hints: Look for the largest heading option.

wrongHints.Apply 'Title': Title works visually, but Docs treats it as the document name — it won't appear as a section in the contents.

steps.intent: Same thing for a section heading — put your cursor on one of the section lines and make it Heading 2. Heading 2 nests underneath Heading 1, which is how the contents gets its indentation.
hints: Open the Styles box again, one step down from Heading 1.

steps.intent: Your turn, no highlight this time. Your headings are set — now insert the table of contents itself. Have a look through the menus.
hints: You're adding something new to the document — which menu handles that?
It's in the Insert menu, near the bottom.
